items.followUp: State two functions of the stem and two functions of the root.

rubric.why: The root system anchors the plant and absorbs water and mineral salts from the soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct root function.

rubric.why: The shoot system bears and supports the aerial parts and carries out functions such as photosynthesis and transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct shoot function.

modelAnswer: The root system anchors the plant in the soil and absorbs water and mineral salts.
The shoot system bears the aerial parts, supports the plant, and carries out functions such as photosynthesis and transport.

items.followUp: Explain what happens to the two male gametes during fertilization in a flowering plant.

rubric.why: Double fertilization is defined by two fusion events occurring in the embryo sac of a flowering plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two fusion events occur in the embryo sac.

rubric.why: The two fusion events result in the formation of a zygote and endosperm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both the zygote and endosperm as outcomes.

modelAnswer: Double fertilization is the occurrence of two fusion events in the embryo sac of a flowering plant.
One male gamete fuses with the egg to form a zygote, while the other fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the endosperm.
